method: VMC (TorFormer, translation-equivariant neural network, total momentum K = 0)
reference: D. D. Dai, Y.-T. Lin & M. Soljačić, Fast, Accurate, and Scalable Fermionic Neural Networks via Translation Equivariance, arXiv:2609.10186
evidence: Table I, N = 91, rs = 30, row TorFormer; sources/2609.10186.txt line 265; printed as (E − E_Mad)/N × rs^(3/2) in Ha
convention_check: Eq. (1) with Ewald summation and a neutralizing background; N = 91 spin-polarized electrons (Sec. II), triangular simulation cell with a1, a2 of equal length at 60° (Sec. III), closed shell, run at K = 0. E_Mad is the classical triangular Wigner-crystal energy, -1.10610258672/rs Ha per electron (QMBL Ewald, checks/heg-hf/hf.mjs madelung() on the one-electron primitive cell); the loader adds it back after dividing by rs^(3/2). Check: the same conversion of the paper's quoted SJB+DMC and Psiformer+SWPA values (Table I, from arXiv:2607.08616) reproduces QMBL's rows from 2607.08616 on both instances to every printed digit. Twist: Gamma (the K = 0 sector of the periodic cell; no twist stated, and the comparison rows from 2607.08616 are Gamma).

compute.reported_as: "Our 212K-parameter TorFormer already has lower energy after 1K steps, and it continues improving over 8K steps." "Training uses a batch size of 2048 and 10K steps for the medium-scale experiments and 8K steps for the large-scale ones." Devices: "eight V100 GPUs, four L40S GPUs, or four H200 GPUs", not stated per run.
